metadata.title: PGSD Eccentricity Demonstration Reproducibility Package v1.1
metadata.description:
Version 1.1 - corrected reference-sphere geometry

This repository provides the data, analysis code, numerical outputs, and documentation required to reproduce the center-eccentricity demonstration presented in the manuscript:

“Physics-Guided Scientific Discovery (PGSD): A Reference Architecture for Explainable Knowledge Generation in Mechanical Engineering.”

Version 1.1 supersedes version 1.0. It corrects the reference-sphere diameter from 24.9984 mm to 24.98484 mm and consequently updates the effective probe-center contact radius to:

R_e = 15.49242 mm.

The original CNC measurement files are preserved unchanged. The correction affects the contact-geometry constants, the constant-radius interpretation, and the calculated higher-order contact scale. It does not change the first-order LFH differential coefficient pair because those coefficients are estimated from the measured-coordinate columns and angular directions.

The demonstration uses two CNC touch-probing acquisitions of the reference sphere, denoted X0Y0 and LT_X0Y0, each containing 32 equatorial measurement points. A nominal relative offset of (-0.300, -0.300) mm was introduced through the CNC/G54 command between the two acquisitions.

The package includes:

  • the original CNC measurement files in CMM format;
  • normalized coordinate datasets;
  • Python scripts for Local Fourier Harmonic analysis and circle fitting;
  • numerical results corresponding to the manuscript;
  • files used to reproduce Figure 4;
  • documentation of the coordinate convention, units, sampling sequence, contact-geometry constants, and execution procedure;
  • a version history and correction note;
  • a package manifest and SHA-256 checksums.

The package reproduces the first-order LFH differential coefficient pair:

  • Delta a1 = -0.299865 mm
  • Delta b1 = -0.300743 mm

and the corresponding provisional inferred magnitude of 0.424695 mm. Using the corrected effective contact radius, the characteristic second-order contact scale is 2.90465 micrometres.

The nominal CNC/G54-commanded offset was not independently measured using an external calibrated displacement reference. Therefore, the numerical differences between the LFH estimate and the nominal command must not be interpreted as independently verified displacement errors. Only one acquisition was available for each state, and no complete uncertainty budget, within-state repeatability study, or multi-state validation was performed. The reported coefficient pair is consequently classified as a physically and operationally corroborated Candidate Signature, not as a validated or canonical Signature.

Changes from version 1.0

  • corrected the reference-sphere diameter to 24.98484 mm;
  • updated the effective contact radius to 15.49242 mm;
  • updated the higher-order contact-scale calculation to 2.90465 micrometres;
  • updated the analysis documentation, numerical metadata, and checksums;
  • preserved the original CMM measurement files;
  • confirmed that the first-order LFH differential coefficients and provisional inverse estimate remain unchanged.

This package supports Section 6 of the PGSD Foundation Preprint v1.2.

metadata.title: AnytimeMonitor: an adaptive controller for TTS-MOS listening tests
metadata.description: AnytimeMonitor is an adaptive controller for Mean Opinion Score (MOS) listening tests in text-to-speech evaluation. It watches a test while it runs and reports, for every pair of systems, whether the accumulated data already supports a verdict — separated, equivalent, or continue — and, when more data is needed, which lever (more items or more listeners) closes the pair fastest. The statistical core is an anytime-valid confidence sequence (Howard, Ramdas, McAuliffe & Sekhon, 2021) on per-item paired score differences, so the analyst may inspect verdicts as often as they like and stop at any data-dependent time while keeping valid coverage. Ships with a Streamlit demo UI (preloaded examples + CSV upload). Research prototype (v0.9) accompanying the paper Doing MOS—and its alternatives—well (Chevelu & Barbot; Computer Speech & Language, Special Issue on the evaluation of speech and speech synthesis).

metadata.description: Mazkur maqolada ingliz va o'zbek masallarini o'zaro tarjima qilish jarayonida allegorik obrazlar va ironik (piching, kesatiq) vositalarning adabiy transpozitsiyasi hamda tarjima adekvatligini ta'minlash masalalari tadqiq etiladi. Masal janriga xos bo'lgan satirik va didaktik xarakter, majoziy obrazlarning milliy-madaniy qatlami va asar tilidagi ironiyaning boshqa dilga ko'chirilish usullari qiyosiy-tarjimashunoslik aspektida tahlil qilingan. Tadqiqot natijalari shuni ko'rsatdiki, allegorik obraz va ironiyani tarjima qilishda shunchaki so'zma-so'z o'girish emas, balki g'oyaviy-badiiy va stilistik qayta yaratish (re-creation) hamda adabiy transpozitsiya tamoyillariga rioya qilish talab etiladi.

metadata.notes:
English abstract

This article examines the issues of literary transposition of allegorical images and ironic devices in the process of translating English and Uzbek fables, with particular emphasis on achieving translation adequacy. The study comparatively analyzes the satirical and didactic nature of the fable genre, the national and cultural specificity of allegorical images, and the methods of conveying irony from the source language into the target language from the perspective of comparative translation studies. The findings indicate that translating allegorical images and irony requires more than a literal rendering; it demands adherence to the principles of artistic and stylistic re-creation, as well as literary transposition, in order to preserve the ideological, aesthetic, and pragmatic value of the original text.

Русская аннотация

В данной статье исследуются вопросы литературной транспозиции аллегорических образов и иронических средств (иронии, насмешки, сарказма) в процессе взаимного перевода английских и узбекских басен, а также проблемы обеспечения адекватности перевода. В сравнительно-переводоведческом аспекте анализируются сатирико-дидактический характер, присущий жанру басни, национально-культурная специфика аллегорических образов и способы передачи иронии художественного текста на другой язык. Результаты исследования показывают, что при переводе аллегорических образов и иронии недостаточно ограничиваться буквальным переводом; необходимо соблюдать принципы идейно-художественного и стилистического воссоздания (re-creation), а также литературной транспозиции.

metadata.title: Phenotypic plasticity and cryptic generic enigma in Pleosporales: Establishing Sporidesmioidesaceae fam. nov. and Rostriconidium synnematicum sp. nov. from India
metadata.description: This study reappraised the taxonomy of the genus Rostriconidium, and introduced a new species, Rostriconidium synnematicum, based on an integrated molecular and morphological taxonomic approach. This new taxon is the only synnematous species within Rostriconidium and forms a sister lineage to other Rostriconidium species in Torulaceae, as supported by phylogenetic analyses of ITS, LSU, SSU, rpb2 and tef1-α sequences using Maximum Likelihood and Bayesian Inference methods. Additionally, a new combination Rostriconidium yunnanensis is proposed under Rostriconidium. The study addresses the taxonomic complexities of four morphologically similar but phylogenetically distinct genera (Neopodoconis, Pseudohelminthosporium, Rostriconidium, and Sporidesmioides) within the Pleosporales. There are a few taxonomic challenges in resolving relationships among these genera, given their polyphyletic nature and overlapping morphologies. In this study, advanced mycological studies were conducted to resolve the generic circumscription of Sporidesmioides. In this study, we propose a new familial lineage, Sporidesmioidesaceae, to accommodate the monotypic species S. thailandica, based on phylogenetic analyses of a multi-locus dataset (ITS, LSU, SSU, rpb2, and tef1-α). The results also accommodate Pseudohelminthosporium within Neomassarinaceae, rather than accepting the synonymization of Pseudohelminthosporium clematidis under Neopodoconis ampullacea. The conspecific nature of P. clematidis and N. ampullacea warrants a future type-based study to validate them. These findings underscore the critical importance of examining type specimens (morphological and multi-locus sequence analysis) before proposing synonymy among cryptic species and genera. This study also revalidated the placement of the recently proposed family Megacapitulaceae and provided their multigene sequence information.

metadata.title: Two novel species of Sympoventuriaceae from palms in China
metadata.description:
Palm plants (Arecaceae) are widely distributed ornamental hosts in southern China. However, most of these plants are introduced species, and their associated microfungal diversity remains poorly understood. In this study, four strains with morphological affinities to Scolecobasidium and Yunnanomyces (Sympoventuriaceae) were isolated from palm plants in Yunnan Province, China. Two novel species, Scolecobasidium yunnanense and Yunnanomyces didymosporus, are proposed based on morphological observations and separate multi-locus phylogenetic analyses: the phylogeny of Scolecobasidium was constructed from a concatenated ITS + nLSU + tub2 + tef1-α dataset, while analyses for Yunnanomyces within Sympoventuriaceae relied on a combined ITS + nLSU + nrSSU + RPB2 dataset. Scolecobasidium yunnanense is characterized by its branched, septate, thick-walled pale hyphae, erect, unbranched and septate conidiophores often reduced to denticulate conidiogenous cells, and smooth, mostly 2-septate, ellipsoidal to fusiform conidia, measuring 8.3–12.6 × 2.0–3.5 μm. Yunnanomyces didymosporus is characterized by its monilioid mature hyphae, intercalary conidiogenous cells, and chain-forming mostly 1-septate conidia with a dark hilum on one or both ends, measuring 6.1–11.9 × 2.0–4.2 μm.

The study confirms their distinctiveness from extant species within each genus and enhances the understanding of microfungal diversity associated with palms.

metadata.title: Astragalus baimaensis (Fabaceae), a new species from Yunnan, China
metadata.description: Based on an integrative analysis of morphological traits and molecular phylogenetic evidence, a new species of Astragalus (Fabaceae), A. baimaensis B. Jiang & Y. Z. Zhang, discovered during field investigations in the Baima Mountain region, Deqin County, Yunnan Province, China, is formally described. This species is defined by a unique combination of diagnostic morphological characters that unequivocally distinguish it from all previously documented congeners: it is completely glabrous throughout, with narrowly oblong leaflets, yellow flowers, and obliquely ellipsoid, glabrous, inflated legumes. The full chloroplast genome of A. baimaensis is 124,633 bp in length. Phylogenetic reconstructions based on plastid genomic data resolve A. baimaensis as sister to A. tongolensis, whereas analyses of the combined nuclear ITS and plastid (rbcL, matK) multilocus dataset support a closer evolutionary affinity between A. baimaensis and A. chilienshanensis. Despite these close phylogenetic relationships, the new species exhibits a distinct set of consistent morphological differences that clearly distinguish it from both putative relatives. The results highlight the considerable taxonomic value of variation in ovary pubescence within Astragalus and confirm that the presence or absence of trichomes on the ovary represents a stable diagnostic trait for species delimitation and infrageneric classification in this genus. This study adds to the known diversity of Astragalus and provides data for future phylogenetic and ecological studies.

metadata.title: THE IMPORTANCE OF PEDAGOGICAL APPROACHES AND MODERN TEACHING METHODS IN ARCHITECTURAL EDUCATION
metadata.description: This article examines how the integration of classical pedagogical theories and contemporary digital tools enhances the development of professional competencies among future architects. Architectural education possesses unique characteristics, combining technical knowledge, artistic and aesthetic understanding, creative thinking, and practical skills. The study addresses the following research question: How can established educational theories and innovative technologies be synthesized to improve the quality of architectural pedagogy? The paper discusses the fundamental principles of pedagogy in architectural education, including visual learning, practice-oriented instruction, the development of independent thinking, project-based learning, and the application of digital technologies. Drawing on published case-study evidence on Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Virtual Reality (VR) in design education, the paper argues that digital tools improve learning outcomes only when integrated within the studio sequence rather than taught as stand-alone technical subjects, and concludes with recommendations for curriculum design.
keywords: architectural education; pedagogical approaches; professional competence; project-based learning; creative thinking; innovative technologies; BIM; 3D modeling; practical training; reflective practice; experiential learning.
